title: Would the compiler let this class extend that one?

blocks.text: The page lists which classes may extend which:

items: a `sealed` class permits exactly the subclasses it names in `permits`, or, with no `permits` clause, exactly the subclasses declared in its own file; any other class trying to extend it fails with `class is not allowed to extend sealed class: <Name>`;
a `final` class may not be extended at all (`cannot inherit from final <Name>`);
a `non-sealed` class, like any plain class, may be extended by anyone.

blocks.text: Write `static String verdict(Class<?> parent, Class<?> candidate)` that answers, from `parent`'s declaration read by reflection, whether the compiler would accept `candidate` as a **direct** subclass of `parent`:

items: return `null` when it would be accepted;
return `"cannot inherit from final " + parent's simple name` when `parent` is final;
return `"class is not allowed to extend sealed class: " + parent's simple name` when `parent` is sealed and does not permit `candidate`.

blocks.text: Only `parent`'s own declaration decides. `Class.isSealed()` and `Class.getPermittedSubclasses()` see both explicit and implicit permits.
**Examples** (with `sealed class Shape permits Circle`, `final class Circle extends Shape`)

items: `verdict(Shape.class, Square.class)` -> `"class is not allowed to extend sealed class: Shape"`

cases.says: A subclass a sealed class permits, explicitly or implicitly, is accepted, and so is any subclass of a plain class.
A class a sealed class does not permit is rejected with the page's compiler message.
No class may extend a final class.
A non-sealed class accepts any subclass, though its own parent is sealed.

concepts: Permitted subclasses are listed in a permits clause or, with none, are exactly the subclasses declared in the same file.
A class that a sealed type does not permit, or that extends a final class, is rejected by the compiler.
